This comparison cannot be made on a single, consistent basis, because the firms report qualitatively different AI claims using different scopes, units, and periods: Bank of America's 300-plus approved AI/machine-learning use cases, 114 live generative AI use cases, and 200,000 teammates using AI (BAC-DECK-2026Q2#29; BAC-PR-2026-10-14-01#2) are company-wide rather than advice-delivery-specific; Schwab's 220 use cases (SCHW-TR-2025Q4#18) are also company-wide, while its advice-specific claims center on Charley, Portfolio Insights and Claude for Financial Advisors (SCHW-PR-2026-10-15-01#3); Raymond James reports 10,000 associates using AI and 6,500 Raimond users but describes itself as 'still in early innings' (RJF-TR-2025Q4#89; RJF-TR-2026Q2#33; RJF-TR-2025Q3#79); and Morgan Stanley reports fewer aggregate figures but makes the most emphatic verbal claims.
